concerns.text: The inline sensitivity approach reuses the same 1,000 block shuffles but only changes zero-position mapping. This does NOT generate a true null distribution under the perturbed zero-density; it conflates the permutation randomness with the zero-density perturbation. A valid sensitivity test requires independent permutation samples under each perturbed zero-count, not reuse of the same shuffle indices.

The 2.5 h estimate for '1,000 permutations × 60 windows × (10⁵ / 100) block shuffles, with inline sensitivity' assumes the inline approach adds negligible cost. However, recomputing quantiles for ±5% and ±10% perturbations (6 variants per window) on the same shuffles is not a true sensitivity analysis and will underestimate the actual computational burden if corrected to use independent permutation samples.

The phrase 'recomputing the permutation quantiles with the adjusted zero count, but using the SAME random shuffles' is mathematically incoherent. Quantiles depend on the distribution of permuted values; if zero-density changes, the permutation distribution changes, and reusing the same shuffle indices does not produce valid quantiles under the new zero-density.

FR-007 requires 'sensitivity analysis on the zero-density parameter by re-running the permutation test with zero-counts adjusted by ±5% and ±10%'. The plan's inline approach does not re-run the permutation test; it reuses shuffles. This violates the requirement.

The research.md states 'The same 1,000 block shuffles are reused; only the mapping of zeros to positions changes.' This is not a valid permutation test under a different zero-density. A permutation test requires sampling from the null distribution; reusing shuffle indices with a different zero-mapping does not sample from the perturbed null.

The fallback to down-sample windows from 20 to 10 per L is mentioned, but the plan does not specify how this affects the statistical power for SC-005 (uniformity of p-value distribution). Reducing from ~3,600 to ~1,800 tests may compromise the KS test's ability to detect non-uniformity.

The plan states 'Sampling uses a fixed seed (seed=20231017)' but does not specify the sampling method (stratified, random, systematic). The data-model.md and research.md do not clarify how the 20 windows per L are selected from the 10⁷ sequence.

The estimate '2.5 h (vectorized NumPy; sensitivity reuses the same shuffles without additional passes)' parenthetical is misleading because the inline approach is not a valid sensitivity analysis, so the time savings claim is moot.
